summary.headline: Nuvama Q2 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY to about INR937 crores and operating PAT 26% to INR319 crores, with ROE near 29%.
summary.overview: Revenue of about INR937 crores (+21% YoY) and operating PAT of about INR319 crores (+26% YoY) were driven by all segments, with Asset Services and Capital Markets contributing strongly. Client assets reached about INR5.5 lakh crores (+25%), with record net new money of INR3,300 crores in Wealth and INR5,000 crores in Private. A one-time post-tax charge of about INR16 crores came from pre-closing a venture debt fund, plus about INR9-10 crores of accelerated amortisation over 12 months. The board skipped the H1 FY27 dividend to manage debt-to-equity, currently about 2.9x against a 2.5x target.

financial_highlights.metric: One-time exceptional charge (venture debt fund pre-closure)

segments.name: Nuvama Wealth (MPIS)
segments.commentary: Client assets crossed about INR46,000 crores; Q2 net flows about INR3,300 crores and over INR6,000 crores in H1. Revenue growth was above 25% YoY in each of seven or eight quarters, moderated this quarter by a high base from a Q2 FY26 real estate co-invest. Lending book about INR6,000 crores, up about 60% YoY.

segments.name: Nuvama Private (ARR)
segments.commentary: ARR assets about INR60,000-62,000 crores; Q2 net new money about INR5,000 crores. ARR is about 64% of revenue. Lending book grew about 50% on H1 basis with NII up about 50%. Transaction income of INR80-90 crores per quarter treated as run rate.

segments.name: Asset Management
segments.commentary: AUM about INR12,000 crores. Commercial real estate fund about 50-55% committed; second fund targets INR5,000 crores. Private credit fund targets INR1,500-2,500 crores. Public markets still loss-making due to AIF-to-SIF transition costs.

segments.name: Asset Services
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR245 crores (+53% YoY) on a low base; client assets INR1.63 lakh crores. Clearing yield moderated to about 2.5% in Q2 from normalisation of cash collateral in new clients.

segments.name: Capital Markets
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR175 crores (+9% YoY). ECM rebounded with IPOs above INR400 crores rising from 4 in Q1 to 38 in Q2; institutional broking hit by CAS impact of about INR2-3 crores per month in Aug-Sep.

guidance_outlook: Wealth and Private cost-to-income expected to improve 100-200 bps YoY this year and continue for at least two more years.
Full-year BAU opex about INR520-530 crores vs INR464 crores last year; with new BKC HO rent-free ROU charge of about INR25 crores, FY27 opex about INR550 crores.
ESAR scheme adds about INR20 crores per quarter to employee cost for next four quarters.
Clearing yield expected between 2.5% and 2.8% for next two years; full-year FY27 around 2.6-2.8%.
Client asset and focus-asset growth guided at 20-25%; Domestic custody business expected to grow about 20%.
Asset Management cost-to-income improvement expected after 12-15 months as new funds are deployed.
capex_capacity: Second commercial real estate fund to launch in about two weeks targeting INR5,000 crores; first fund about 50-55% committed.
Private credit fund (performing / special situations, 15-18% target return) to launch in 25-30 days, targeting INR1,500-2,500 crores over 8-10 months.
SIF launch expected in 25-30 days after approval received; private equity new fund planned for Q3 or Q4 or next year.
RTA for AIFs and PMSs to go live with minimum proposition by end-November or December; full scale by March. Trustee services between Q3 and Q4.
Added about 250 employees over 12 months (85-90% business-facing); about 90 RMs in Wealth and 14-15 RMs in Private added over the past year.
demand_pricing: Primary market activity jumped: IPOs above INR400 crores went from 4 in Q1 to 38 in Q2; pipeline of about 40 IB transactions (30 ECM, 9 advisory) with probability-adjusted revenue of INR85-90 crores.
ECM participation share about 15-18% of transactions; weaker in blocks, stronger in QIPs and IPOs.
Domestic PMS market share about 6-7% and AIF about 8-9% of book; capture about 25% of new domestic registrations.
Monetisation clients contributed about 35-38% of net new money over last 15 months.
Insurance is about 12-13% of Wealth revenue and zero in Private.
Competition: about 18-19 competitors in custody/clearing; new domestic custodian licences expected over the next two years.
Q2 cash volume down about 12% QoQ from CAS impact in secondary markets.

qa_highlights.question: Is the AMC one-time loss due to committed returns to investors?
qa_highlights.answer: No. It is unamortised upfront distribution cost on a venture fund pre-wound; for a INR1,000 crore fund with INR300 crore called, the INR700 crore balance is written off. Further INR8-10 crore accelerated amortisation over 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Will Anugrah-related surplus capital be released?
qa_highlights.answer: Excess capital was limited; a INR500 crore bank guarantee needed only about INR125-130 crore cash, which will be redeployed in clearing or other businesses.

qa_highlights.question: Is the custody/clearing yield decline a threat from new domestic licences?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees about 18-19 competitors already; new licence holders are mostly asset managers. Clearing yield depends on cash vs G-sec mix (currently 38-40% cash) and is expected at 2.5-2.8% for two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will debt-to-equity restrict lending growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 2.5x from 2.9x; at 2.5x with about INR1,000-1,300 crore annual profit, around INR3,000-4,000 crore of incremental lending headroom is possible, so internal accruals may suffice. Dividend payout policy under board review.

qa_highlights.question: Clarification on PAG stake sale?
qa_highlights.answer: Nothing as of now; the process is being done by shareholders, and the company will disclose anything material.

risks_watch: Debt-to-equity at about 2.9x vs 2.5x target; rating and covenant pressure if leverage rises further; dividend policy to be reviewed with FY27 annual results (April 2027).
Asset Management cost burden from SIF, private credit and PE team build-up; cost-income improvement not expected for 12-15 months.
Clearing yield sensitivity to cash/G-sec mix and FPI collateral growth; competitive pressure from new custodian licences.
Q2 capital markets institutional broking hit by CAS; expected to reverse from December.
Wealth attrition: one team movement with about 75-80% arrested; no revenue impact expected.
Non-recurring items: INR9-10 crore amortisation over next 12 months and ESAR charge of INR20 crore per quarter for four quarters.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, flows and primary market recovery, while cautious on balance sheet and Asset Management cost. Management was candid that Q2 transaction income had a high base effect and that Q1 fixed-income gains will not recur.
key_quotes: Just to summarize, we delivered a reasonably good quarter of strong performance.
Client assets now are about INR5.5 lakh crores. Revenue was about INR937 crores. Operating PAT about INR319 crores, with a yearly growth of 26%.
If I take Q1 plus Q2 put together, we are about 11% to 12% of the opening balance, and our guidance has always been that we will be between 22% to 25%, which I think we are on track.
We will have to look at the dividends and maybe see whether we overall continue with that 40%-60% payout, because that can now become detrimental for shareholders.

adds.what: Second commercial real estate fund targeting INR5,000 crore (first fund ~50-55% committed)
Private credit fund targeting INR1,500-2,500 crore over 8-10 months
SIF launch pending approval, expected in 25-30 days
RTA for AIFs and PMSs go-live with minimum proposition by end-Nov/Dec, full scale by March

growth.why: Q2 revenue +21% and operating PAT +26% YoY with client asset growth guided at 20-25% and clearing yield 2.6-2.8%, backed partly by new funds (INR5,000 cr CRE fund, INR1,500-2,500 cr private credit fund), SIF and RTA launches, and a 250-employee hiring plan; full-year opex raised to ~INR550 cr.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides Wealth and Private cost-to-income to improve 100-200 bps YoY this year, but FY27 opex rises to about INR550 crore (BAU INR520-530 crore plus ~INR25 crore ROU charge) and ESAR adds about INR20 crore per quarter for four quarters, so the margin gain is conditional on revenue keeping pace.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Second CRE fund (INR5,000 crore target, first fund 50-55% committed), private credit fund (INR1,500-2,500 crore over 8-10 months), SIF and RTA go-live are all firmly scheduled within 1-2 quarters, and about 250 employees were added over 12 months.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Client asset and focus-asset growth guided at 20-25%, Q2 net new money about INR3,300 crore in Wealth and INR5,000 crore in Private, and client assets about INR5.5 lakh crore (+25%).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed as such; new asset-management funds and the PE fund (planned Q3 to Q4 or next year) are the nearest equivalent, with debt-to-equity at 2.9x against a 2.5x target limiting balance-sheet-funded expansion.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q2 revenue rose 21% YoY and operating PAT 26%, but management flagged a high Q2 base, non-recurring Q1 fixed-income gains and CAS-hit institutional broking, so upside is conditional on IPO and ECM momentum (IPOs above INR400 crore rose from 4 to 38 QoQ).

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Clearing yield is guided at 2.6-2.8% for FY27 against 2.5% in Q2, FY27 opex is raised to about INR550 crore, and debt-to-equity at 2.9x sits above the 2.5x target; Asset Management costs are not expected to improve for 12-15 months.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Private credit fund launch in 25-30 days, SIF launch in 25-30 days after approval, second CRE fund launch in about two weeks, and RTA go-live for AIFs and PMSs by end-November or December.

rows.label: Primary market / IPO pipeline recovery
rows.why: IPOs above INR400 crore rose from 4 in Q1 to 38 in Q2, and about 40 IB transactions with probability-adjusted revenue of INR85-90 crore are in the pipeline.

rows.label: Debt-to-equity back to 2.5x target
rows.why: Debt-to-equity is about 2.9x against a 2.5x target, and about INR1,000-1,300 crore of annual profit gives roughly INR3,000-4,000 crore of lending headroom, so internal accruals may suffice; the H1 FY27 dividend was skipped and policy is under review.

rows.label: Asset Management cost-to-income improvement
rows.why: Public markets are still loss-making on AIF-to-SIF transition costs, and an INR8-10 crore accelerated amortisation runs over the next 12 months, so the benefit only comes as new funds are deployed.

tone.note: Management was confident on flows, client assets and the primary-market recovery, and cautious on the 2.9x debt-to-equity, Asset Management cost burden and clearing-yield compression; analysts probed the AMC one-time charge, the leverage headroom and the PAG stake sale.
